cards.text: Jeremiah, God's prophet, is passing along a message from the LORD to His people, the house of Israel and the house of Judah. It opens the way good news SHOULD open: 'The days are coming'. Friend, I sat in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS waiting for somebody to say that to me.

cards.question: The LORD says He will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with seed. What kind of seed?

answers.text: The seed of man and of beast
The seed of wheat and barley
The seed of the olive and vine

cards.question: The LORD watched over His people to uproot and tear down. Now He says He'll watch over them to ___ and to ___.

cards.text: In those days, the LORD says, people will stop repeating an old saying: 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge.' Dad eats the sour grapes, and the KIDS are the ones making the face.

cards.question: True or false: Once that old saying is gone, each person will die for his own iniquity.

cards.text: Then the LORD says it: He will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. NEW, friend, and trust me, I know new when I see it, because a shiny new stamper took my spot on the counter.

cards.question: This new covenant won't be like the one the LORD made with their fathers when He took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of ___.

cards.text: And here's the part that stings. They broke that covenant, the LORD says, though He was a husband to them.

cards.question: So what makes the new covenant different? Where will the LORD put His law this time?

answers.text: In their minds and on their hearts
On the doorposts of their houses

cards.text: Then the LORD promises, 'And I will be their God, and they will be My people.' I'm getting misty over here, friend, and I'm a COOKIE STAMPER.

cards.question: In those days, no one will need to teach his neighbor or his brother to know the LORD. Why not?

answers.text: The law will be read aloud

cards.question: True or false: In the new covenant, only the greatest among the people will know the LORD.
The LORD says He will forgive their iniquities. And what will He do with their sins?

cards.text: Then the LORD tells who He is: He gives the sun for light by day, sets the moon and stars in order for night, and stirs up the sea so its waves roar. The LORD of Hosts runs ALL of that, and I lost my oven timer twice this week.

cards.question: The LORD calls the sun, moon, stars and sea a fixed order. When would Israel's descendants stop being a nation before Him?

answers.text: Only if that fixed order departed
If they broke His covenant again

cards.text: Then the LORD gives a second picture, about measuring the heavens above and searching out the foundations of the earth below. Friend, I can't measure the sugar for ONE batch without spilling half of it.

cards.question: Only if the heavens could be measured and the earth's foundations searched out, the LORD says, would He ___ all of Israel's descendants because of all they have done.

cards.text: Last, the LORD says the days are coming when this city, Jerusalem, will be rebuilt for Him, with the measuring line stretched from the tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate and out to the Kidron Valley. Even the valley of the dead bodies and ashes will be holy to the LORD.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says the rebuilt city will one day be uprooted and demolished again.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The card says the message is spoken 'to His people, the house of Israel and the house of Judah.' In 31:27 the LORD speaks about the house of Israel and the house of Judah in the third person ('I will sow the house of Israel'). The text doesn't say they are the ones being spoken to, so the card fills in the audience.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question brings in the phrase 'a fixed order,' and only the right answer repeats it ('Only if that fixed order departed'). The echo, plus the more Bible-sounding 'departed,' makes the right answer stand out from the other two.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card says the measuring line is stretched from the tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate and out to the Kidron Valley. The text says something different. The city is rebuilt from the tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate (31:38). The measuring line stretches to the hill of Gareb and turns toward Goah (31:39). The fields as far as the Kidron Valley are what will be holy (31:40). The card joins these into one measuring line the text doesn't describe.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Card 18 treats 31:38-40 (the city's boundaries) as a long stretch and sums it up in one story card. Card 19 then asks a choice card about 31:40, which is inside that stretch. If the 'never again uprooted or demolished' promise is meant to be asked, it should be split out of the stretch. Otherwise it should only appear as the standout detail on the summary card.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: The joke compares the LORD's new covenant to the shiny new stamper that replaced Papa Dorin and sent him to the junk drawer. The comparison follows the same action (new replacing old), but in his story that replacement is a sad loss. The joke may suggest the first covenant was set aside for being worn out. The text says the new covenant differs because the people broke the old one (31:32).
findings.question: Is it acceptable to compare God's new covenant to the replacement stamper from Papa Dorin's sad backstory, or should the comparison use a different image, such as his own renewal by the One who makes things new?
